ratings.concept: Milk dentition: incisors, canines and molars are present, premolars are not

traps.label: true_statement_trap
traps.route: Reads past the "not". Children have incisors from the first set onwards.

traps.label: true_statement_trap
traps.route: Reads past the "not". Milk canines are present and are later replaced.

traps.label: true_statement_trap
traps.route: Mixes up which teeth replace which. Milk molars are present, and premolars are what replace them.

ratings.concept: Protoplast: a cell stripped of its wall, with the plasma membrane and contents intact

ratings.concept: Diatom frustule: a silica wall in two overlapping halves that fit like a soap-box

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: A slime-mould plasmodium is a naked mass of protoplasm. With no wall there are no shells to overlap.

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: Euglenoids have a protein pellicle rather than a cell wall. Again there is nothing that could split into two halves.

traps.label: other_one_fact
traps.route: Reaches for the stiff cellulose plates of dinoflagellates. Those are many small plates, not two halves that fit together.

ratings.reason: This question requires one stored diagnostic feature, demonstrated by the stem's "two thin overlapping shells which fit together", which describes the diatom frustule and nothing else.

ratings.concept: Cloning vector: the DNA molecule that carries the gene of interest into a host cell

traps.label: look_alike_term
traps.route: Uses the everyday word for what a vector does. "Carrier" describes the job but is not the term for the molecule.

traps.label: fabricated_term
traps.route: Builds a word out of "transformation", the step that puts recombinant DNA into the host. No molecule called a transformer appears in the chapter.

traps.label: true_but_out_of_scope
traps.route: Answers for DNA replication instead. A template is the strand that gets copied, not the molecule a gene is inserted into.

ratings.reason: This question requires one stored definition, demonstrated by the stem's "to which the gene of interest is integrated for cloning", which is the defining description of a vector.

ratings.concept: Male gametophyte of angiosperms: the pollen grain gives two sperms and one vegetative cell

traps.label: calculation_slip
traps.route: Counts all three cells of the pollen grain as sperms. Gives three instead of two sperms and one vegetative cell.

traps.label: intermediate_value
traps.route: Stops at the two-celled pollen grain as it is shed. The generative cell has not yet divided into the two sperms at that stage.

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: A pollen grain carries one vegetative cell at every stage. Two of them never occur.

ratings.reason: This question requires one stored composition recalled whole, demonstrated by the option "Single sperm and a vegetative cell" failing on its first half alone while its second half matches the key.
ratings.note: E2 is pick_both_parts rather than name_or_identify because the four options vary the sperm count and the vegetative-cell count independently - 3 and 0, 2 and 1, 1 and 1, 1 and 2 - so both halves of the answer have to hold.

ratings.concept: Coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm; the white kernel is the cellular endosperm formed later

traps.label: other_one_fact
traps.route: Reaches for perisperm, the leftover nucellus. That is the dry tissue of beet and black pepper, not a liquid.

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: The embryo is a small solid body sitting in the kernel. It is never the liquid the stem asks about.

traps.label: no_derivation_route
traps.route: The seed coat is the thin brown layer against the shell. Nothing about it is liquid.

ratings.reason: This question requires one stored example, demonstrated by the stem's "Coconut water from a tender coconut", the textbook instance of free-nuclear endosperm.
